  status: active           # pending S1
  budget_ms: 0.3
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  notes: "one rects_in over a 288x288 px box on a static_version change (TR-section-016); charged inside ADR-0017's EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS, not added to the hook ledger; probed 34 us on the editor binary, not a pass"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"performance_budgets","name":"layout_geom_overlap_uncached","entry_yaml":"- system: layout_geom_overlap_uncached
  status: active           # pending S1 (V4)
  budget_ms: 2.0
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  notes: "target owned by ADR-0013 can_attach (2 ms or less, uncached); ADR-0014 contributes the footprint_overlaps rect leg and S1 measures both legs (rect leg here, tile-cell leg is ADR-0013's floor_tile_at check) at the largest MVP body pair; worst-case rect-leg estimate about 6 ms for 2,000 probes at about 3 us on the editor binary, UNVERIFIED"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"one_rect_set_row_table","entry_yaml":"- purpose: one_rect_set_row_table
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed; pass lines pending S1
  api: "one derived row table per LIVE body in ascending (section_id, idx) order = ascending rect_key; dense CSR uniform grid (BROADPHASE_CELL_PX) of row numbers; leaf, PLATE and JAMB slots inserted at maximum footprint, layout.doors writes only the row's current extent via set_extent (hot); empty extent is the EXTENT_EMPTY_LO/HI sentinel; rects_in and solid_in are OCCLUDES_LIGHT and SOLID masks over the same table; the tile-cell leg of GEOM_OVERLAP is not in this table (ADR-0013 floor_tile_at check); rebuilt synchronously as the last step of LM1-LM4 and restore"
  not: "a second rect copy or per-consumer index; an Emitter-owned rect index; engine physics, PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D or TileSet physics/occlusion/navigation layers as a rect source; a separate dynamic leaf list; a Dictionary-keyed grid; a perceived or phantom variant of any geometry query"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  reason: "Pillar 1 (collision, light and drawing cannot disagree); structural key order needs no sort; door animation changes no grid"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"caller_owned_query_buffer","entry_yaml":"- purpose: caller_owned_query_buffer
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  api: "hot geometry queries are out-parameter calls into a consumer-owned QueryBuffer (overwrite, count authoritative, public SoA columns, no set( accessor); box is four half-open ints plus an explicit body_id; return value is the record count; overflow calls the cold untagged geometric grow() (counted, never truncates) and steady state means grew == 0"
  not: "Rect2i box arguments; a value-returning rects_in; a shared buffer returned by Layout; resize/append/array construction inside a ## @hot query; reading at or beyond count; keeping out.keys/spans/flags beyond the call; one buffer for two live results; passing out.keys/spans/flags by value to a native method inside a hot function"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  reason: "aliasing between Body, Emitter, Lighting within one tick (AC-151); HOT-01 + CNT-01 + CNT-02 allocation wording; probed alias write-through and shrink/grow zero-fill"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"occupied_span_single_conversion","entry_yaml":"- purpose: occupied_span_single_conversion
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  api: "QueryBuffer.spans hold OCCUPIED (closed) spans (x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1) in the body frame; a half-open consumer decodes in exactly one inline helper: x1 = spans[4k+2] + 1, y1 = spans[4k+3] + 1; a polygon builder places corners at (x0, y0) and (x1_occ+1, y1_occ+1); Layout applies no shift; CollideSource/LayoutCollide (ADR-0015) is the only wrapper over SolidQuery"
  not: "reading spans[4k+2] or spans[4k+3] as a half-open bound (shrinks every rect 1 px on its high edges); a second decode site; a Layout-side shift"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  reason: "a 1-px shrink lets an actor enter a wall and leaves a 1-px seam between abutting hull rects, and a 1-px light leak at every wall edge (Pillar 1)"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"layout_version_counters","entry_yaml":"- purpose: layout_version_counters
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  api: "per-section int64 version/static_version/leaf_version in private columns behind bounds-guarded getters (compare for inequality only; 0 = no live section; invalidate to 0 on discard; at restore every LIVE section is 1 and every other section 0); non-persisted version_epoch incremented by restore and default_state (new_epoch also resets every changed_region stamp_tick to -1), consumers cache (version_epoch, version) and an epoch change gates only result-neutral cache rebuilds; changed_region is simulation-side, lazily valid only when stamp_tick == ClockView.tick(), merge lattice ALL > REGION(union) > FRAME, advisory after a restore"
  not: "persisting or hashing a counter, stamp or version_epoch; a presentation read of changed_region; relying on changed_region == ALL after a restore; reusing 0 for a live section; confusing version_epoch with restore_epoch; feeding a version_epoch change into a work budget, persisted value or RNG draw"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  reason: "a reset-to-1 version can equal a stale cached value after restore; the epoch closes it in the type"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"broadphase_cell_coupling","entry_yaml":"- purpose: broadphase_cell_coupling
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  api: "BOOT-tier named invariant BROADPHASE_CELL_COUPLING (CONTENT_INVARIANT, domain 2): BROADPHASE_CELL_PX >= max(FOOT_BOX_W, FOOT_BOX_H) + V_RUN, evaluated at ContentLoader stage 4 by the pure helper BroadphaseCoupling.holds in src/shared/layout/; sole owner of TR-shipbody-037 (ADR-0015 carries no separate BODY_BROADPHASE_CELL); companion BOOT invariant WORLD_COORD_LIMIT_BELOW_SENTINEL (WORLD_COORD_LIMIT < EXTENT_EMPTY_LO, BroadphaseCoupling.sentinel_clear; ADR-0007 registration ask); protects the 4-cell cost bound only, queries are correct at any positive cell size"
  not: "treating it as an advisory range; clamping the cell size; hard-coding the constant 3 for V_RUN; a second cell-size invariant in Body"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  reason: "TR-shipbody-037; a swept foot box of width at most FOOT_BOX_W + V_RUN touches at most 2 cells per axis iff cell >= that width; packed int32 writes truncate silently so coordinates must stay far from the sentinels"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"engine_collision_or_tileset_as_rect_source","entry_yaml":"- pattern: engine_collision_or_tileset_as_rect_source
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  description: "No PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D, shape query, CharacterBody2D/Area2D, TileSet physics/occlusion/navigation layer or LightOccluder2D is a source of collision, occlusion or footprint rectangles; the PROJECTOR and the occluder builder draw from Layout's rect set, never the reverse."
  why: "TR-section-011 / TR-light-035: one rect set; engine physics is non-deterministic and tree-bound; a TileSet occluder layer carries one mask per layer."
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"shared_or_returned_query_buffer","entry_yaml":"- pattern: shared_or_returned_query_buffer
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  description: "A geometry query never returns an array or a Layout-owned buffer; every consumer passes its own QueryBuffer, never stores its columns beyond the call that filled them and never shares one buffer between two live results."
  why: "A shared returned buffer aliases between Body, Emitter, Lighting and Interaction within one tick and cannot be both allocation-free and copy-on-write safe (LY-12 e, AC-151)."
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"perceived_variant_of_geometry_query","entry_yaml":"- pattern: perceived_variant_of_geometry_query
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  description: "rects_in, solid_in, solid_at and section_rects_into have no perceived, phantom or lying variant; a hallucination never changes what a wall or door leaf is for collision or occlusion."
  why: "Pillar 1 / TR-section-011: the world never lies; only instruments and perception can."
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"changed_region_read_outside_its_tick","entry_yaml":"- pattern: changed_region_read_outside_its_tick
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  description: "changed_region is a simulation-side read valid only in the tick it was stamped; presentation never reads it (it keys on version_epoch, version and the dirty batch), and no consumer relies on changed_region == ALL after a restore (it is advisory there; version_epoch is the restore signal)."
  why: "A rendered frame can follow up to four ticks, and a stamp written in post_restore does not match the first RUNNING tick's T (ADR-0016 section 1.1, OQ-1 closed)."
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"half_open_read_of_occupied_span","entry_yaml":"- pattern: half_open_read_of_occupied_span
  status: active           # ADR-0014 is Proposed
  description: "No consumer reads QueryBuffer.spans[4k+2] or spans[4k+3] as a half-open x1/y1; the conversion (+ 1) happens in one inline helper, and SolidQuery is wrapped only by CollideSource/LayoutCollide."
  why: "A 1-px shrink on high edges lets an actor enter a wall, leaves a 1-px seam between abutting hull rects and a 1-px light leak."
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md
  added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"interface_mechanism","entry_yaml":"# interface_mechanism (append to the existing entry's referenced_by)
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"allocation_verification","entry_yaml":"# allocation_verification (append to the existing entry's referenced_by)
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked","entry_yaml":"# packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked (append to the existing entry's referenced_by; the QueryBuffer out-record exemption is a Foundation ask)
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"integer_division_convention","entry_yaml":"# integer_division_convention (append to the existing entry's referenced_by)
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"native_code_policy","entry_yaml":"# native_code_policy (append to the existing entry's referenced_by)
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"physics_callback_tick_source","entry_yaml":"# physics_callback_tick_source and scene_tree_or_engine_server_in_sim_layers (append to both existing entries' referenced_by)
    - docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md"}]},{"adr":"ADR-0015","items":[{"section":"state_ownership","name":"body_state","entry_yaml":"- state: body_state
  status: active           # ADR-0015 is Proposed
  owner_system: ship-body-and-interior-physics (BodyModule)
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  interface: "block body.state (SIM, WORLD, SHARED, gameplay, interpolated, restore_after [layout.state], fault domain 5); persisted: next_actor_id, per-actor {actor_id, kind SEAT=1/AGENT=2, seat, body_id, pos_curr, sub, last_octant, odometer}, sparse per-body {body_id, world_x, world_y, vel_x, vel_y, heading_q}; every int32 column value range-checked before write (body_id 1..2^31-1, seat 0..MAX_SEAT, pos within BODY_COORD_LIMIT); derived and never persisted or hashed: pos_prev, blocked, world_prev; read only through BodyView"
  write_access: body.integrate hook and mutators BM1-BM8 only (called from Assembly, Transit or Web Map apply after the Layout mutator; BM8 release_body after LM4)
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"body_mutators","entry_yaml":"- contract: body_mutators
  status: active
  pattern: direct_call
  producer: ship-body-and-interior-physics
  consumers: [modular-ship-assembly, web-map-and-transit, derelict-authoring]
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  signal_signature: "Class A: can_x(views, args) -> StringName (&\"\" = OK, BodyReasons) and x(scope, args, [out]) -> int (OK 0, REFUSED 1, -BodyFaults code, domain 5); place_actor(scope, body_id, x, y, kind, seat, out: PlaceResult), remove_actor, rebase_on_attach(scope, surviving, absorbed, shift_x, shift_y, moved_sections: PackedInt32Array) with can_rebase_attach (both LIVE, before LM2) and apply-time absorbed DISSOLVED (after LM2), rebase_on_detach(scope, old, new, moved_sections, shift_x, shift_y, cap_rects: PackedInt32Array) with can_rebase_detach(views, old, shift_x, shift_y, cap_rects) returning BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP, transfer_actor(scope, actor_id, to_body_id, x, y, cause), set_body_velocity, set_body_pose, release_body(scope, body_id) / can_release_body (BM8: deletes the pose row of a DISSOLVED body after LM4, refuses while actors remain); check-then-write; defects call PlanMismatchSink.report then scope.fault; BM4 pose or velocity saturation returns OK and does not fault; BM4 inserts the new pose row only if not canonical-empty""},{"section":"interfaces","name":"locomotion_step","entry_yaml":"- contract: locomotion_step
  status: active
  pattern: direct_call
  producer: ship-body-and-interior-physics (src/sim/body/locomotion/)
  consumers: [ship-body-and-interior-physics, horror-entities]
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  signal_signature: "LocomotionStep(v_eff_max, decel_ladder_enabled).step(state: LocoState, intent: LocoIntent, collide: CollideSource) -> LocoResult and step_into(state, intent, collide, out: LocoResult) -> void with identical results; LocoState carries body_id (the frame, never written by step); pure RefCounted; trunc_div for the residue, floor_div only px-to-tile; octant NONE returns before any table index; CollideSource (@abstract, Body-side port wrapping ADR-0014 SolidQuery via LayoutCollide) query_into(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out: QueryBuffer) -> int and origin_in_body(body_id, x, y) -> bool, no bind; QueryBuffer spans are inclusive and decoded only by RectSpans""},{"section":"interfaces","name":"body_read_view","entry_yaml":"- contract: body_read_view
  status: active
  pattern: direct_call
  producer: ship-body-and-interior-physics
  consumers: [suit, interaction, emitter, lighting, controller.noise, controller, assembly, web-map-and-transit, body.projector, presentation]
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  signal_signature: "BodyView (long-lived getter-only facade plus empty twin; neutral values for unknown actor or body via _find_actor_row == -1): pos_x/_y, prev_x/_y (scalars; a Vector2i only at an adapter boundary), body_of_actor, seat_of_actor, actor_of_seat, foot_boxes_into (ascending, unfiltered), actor_section/actor_local_x/_y (derived on demand, never cached), actors_overlapping_into, actors_on_into, world_*/vel_*/world_prev_*, docked, body_count, odometer, trapped_into, moved_x/_y (SIM only from a hook after body.integrate), blocked (a_blocked != 0; presentation and diagnostic only)""},{"section":"interfaces","name":"body_events","entry_yaml":"- contract: body_events
  status: active
  pattern: observer
  producer: ship-body-and-interior-physics
  consumers: [pipeline, body.projector, adaptive-audio, controller-diagnostics]
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  signal_signature: "scope.emit_event(&body.state, kind, a0..a5): BODY_TRANSFER=1 (actor_id, old_body, new_body, frame_delta_x, frame_delta_y, cause WELD 1/DETACH 2/POD 3), BODY_DOCK_CONTACT=2 (surviving, absorbed), BODY_HULL_SEPARATION=3 (old, new); dirty-key kinds BODY=2, ACT=4; quiet_writes_allowed=false""},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"swept_analytic_clamp","entry_yaml":"- purpose: actor_collision_sweep
  status: active
  api: "one SolidQuery.solid_in query (via LayoutCollide) per moving actor per tick over the Minkowski cover of the foot box; rectangles decoded from ADR-0014 inclusive spans through RectSpans only (x1 = spans[4k+2] + 1, y1 = spans[4k+3] + 1); per-axis analytic clamp against each returned rectangle's near edge for E-empty actors; exempt actors (start box inside a SOLID rect) use a per-sub-step predicate (non-increasing per-rectangle overlap AND destination origin in a section of the actor's body); stationary actors issue no query; the literal 1-px stepper is the test oracle and a debug cross-check only"
  not: "engine physics bodies or shapes; the 1-px stepper in a release hot path; an inflated margin or second rectangle set; push-out, shove, snap or eject; a stateful bind(body_id) on the collide port; a second span-to-half-open conversion"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  reason: "exact equivalence to the 1-px specification (probed 2026-10-29: 0 mismatches in 300,000 fixtures; scripts to be committed under tests/support/probes/adr-0015/) at about 3K instead of 7K rectangle tests""},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"interpolated_pair_in_hook","entry_yaml":"- purpose: body_interpolated_pair
  status: active
  api: "body.state is interpolated=true; pos_prev and world_prev are derived columns rolled inside body.integrate for every row and inside every discontinuous mutator; commit_baseline is a documented no-op; snap_baseline(_key, ctx) sets prev := curr; post_restore derives prev := curr"
  not: "a P4 roll of the pair (prev == curr at P5 erases interpolation and zeroes moved); a persisted or hashed pos_prev"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  reason: "controller.noise must read this tick's moved after body.integrate; presenters need the last tick's pair at P5""},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"body_snapshot_shape","entry_yaml":"- purpose: body_snapshot_shape
  status: active
  api: "snapshot() is a plain Dictionary with exactly five keys next_actor_id, n_bodies, n_actors, bodies (n*6 plain-Array ints), actors (n*10 plain-Array ints), ascending ids, no floats, no pos_prev; restore validates version, type, count, per-row column ranges (BDY_RESTORE_COLUMN_RANGE before every other per-row check), order/canonicity, Layout LIVE state and reports only through ctx.fault(BDY_RESTORE_*); phase 2 copies element by element and never replaces a column reference; idempotent so body.state is not in REBASE_BLOCKS; in-memory layout is id-sorted SoA (reversible by spike S1 without a schema change)"
  not: "Packed arrays in the payload; var_to_bytes for any hashed byte; an owner byte writer; clamping on restore; a wrapping write into an int32 column"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  reason: "TR-shipbody-008/009/041; the type walk (binary path only) keeps a decoded float from being truncated into a range-valid integer; a PackedInt32Array element write wraps silently""},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"packed_array_const_form","entry_yaml":"- purpose: packed_array_constant_declaration
  status: active
  api: "table constants are declared `const NAME: PackedInt32Array = [..]` (or Array[int]) and treated as read-only; `_find_actor_row`/`_find_body_row` return -1 unless bsearch row < size and id matches; blocked stored as a byte"
  not: "`const NAME := PackedInt32Array([..])` or `PackedInt32Array()` in a const (does not compile on 4.7.2); reading a_id[row] from a raw bsearch index; assigning a bool into a PackedByteArray element"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  reason: "probed on 4.7.2 by the engine review (V9)""},{"section":"performance_budgets","name":"body_integrate_hook","entry_yaml":"- system: body_integrate_hook
  status: active           # ADR-0015 is Proposed; figure pending spike S1
  budget_ms: 0.4
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  notes: "whole body.integrate hook for eight actors (0.05 ms per actor P99), including ADR-0014 solid_in calls, the clamp, the row copy and the dirty marks; S1 reports it with solid_in as a sub-counter; Body's row in the ADR-0003 kernel_p3_step_hooks share ledger (2.0 ms target); not additive with ADR-0014's solid_in figure"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"engine_physics_on_sim_path","entry_yaml":"- pattern: engine_physics_on_sim_path
  status: active
  description: "Any Godot physics body, area, shape, server, physics query (including RayCast2D, ShapeCast2D, KinematicCollision2D, the 2D query-parameter types, CollisionObject2D/Shape2D/Polygon2D, direct_space_state, get_world_2d), engine tile collision (collision_enabled) or navigation mesh referenced from src/sim or src/shared (SIM-06 plus the BDY-01 supplementary tokens); the only future exemption is the presentation-only debris of ADR-0033 on a src/presentation path"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  why: "Position must be a pure function of the command stream and Layout (G3, G4); one rectangle set serves collision, light and drawing; the guarantee is no use, not not-instantiated""},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"actor_displacement","entry_yaml":"- pattern: actor_displacement
  status: active
  description: "Push-out, shove, snap, eject or any unannounced position change of an actor by Body, Layout, Assembly or a hook other than LocomotionStep and the BM3/BM4/BM5 transfer arithmetic"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  why: "Pillar 2 (no unannounced displacement) and PCI:650; a cut that would entomb an actor is refused (BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP, asked by can_rebase_detach for every cut origin), never resolved by ejection""},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"sim_read_of_blocked_or_world","entry_yaml":"- pattern: sim_read_of_blocked_or_world
  status: active
  description: "A SIM hook reading BodyView blocked; a body-frame computation reading world_*/vel_*; a SIM hook not ordered after body.integrate reading moved_* or prev_* (lints BDY-02, BDY-03, BDY-04)"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  why: "blocked would become sim state that must be persisted and hashed; the interior must be byte-identical for a moving and a resting ship; moved is only G4-exact after body.integrate""},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"cached_row_index_across_mutator","entry_yaml":"- pattern: cached_row_index_across_mutator
  status: active
  description: "Holding a body.state row index, an actor_section answer, a Dictionary key or a packed-column alias in a member (BodyView, the hook, LayoutCollide) across a Body mutator or a restore"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md
  why: "Rows are kept id-sorted by insertion and removal, so indices move; restore copies element by element so a member alias would otherwise hold stale data; Suit reads actor_section after a transfer may have run""},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"mutator_status","entry_yaml":"- contract: mutator_status
  add_referenced_by: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"block_persistence_payload","entry_yaml":"- contract: block_persistence_payload
  add_referenced_by: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"integer_division_convention","entry_yaml":"- purpose: integer_division_convention
  add_referenced_by: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"dirty_key_marking","entry_yaml":"- contract: dirty_key_marking
  add_referenced_by: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"canvas_coordinate_exactness","entry_yaml":"- purpose: canvas_coordinate_exactness
  add_referenced_by: docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md   # ADR-0015 section 10 owns BODY_COORD_LIMIT and the canvas bound |world_a - world_b| + |pos| < 2^23"}]},{"adr":"ADR-0016","items":[{"section":"state_ownership","name":"restore_plan","entry_yaml":"  - state: restore_plan
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed; entries become binding when it is Accepted
    owner_system: command-simulation-layer (kernel)
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    interface: "RestorePlan (RefCounted, src/kernel/restore_plan.gd): private _order, _rank, _world_order, _post_order, _bind_order as PackedInt32Arrays read through order_at/rank_of/size and world_*/post_*/bind_* accessors; compiled once at the registry freeze from BlockDescriptor.restore_after by Kahn with smallest-registration-index tie-break (bind_order via CanonicalEncoder.sorted_string_keys); immutable by convention (hash of describe() checked); tests install alternatives through RestorePlan.from_order, which validates a linear extension; H1 allow-list name in the registries group (ADR-0003 section 10 ask)"
    write_access: kernel-only
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: every-block-owner (via restore_after)
    consumers:
      - command-simulation-layer
      - save-load
      - debug-overlay
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"restore_pass_stages","entry_yaml":"  - contract: restore_pass_stages
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: kernel
    consumers:
      - save-load
      - every-persisted-block-owner
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    signal_signature: "LOADING restore pass: R0 flush Dropped(RELOAD); R1 whole-payload pre-check in a fixed order (a payload keys as String ascending with kernel.clock known: RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK; b TICK_RATE_MISMATCH; c RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE; d world_order schema_version: RESTORE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED) with every block, clock and half (b) intact; R2 clock install (ClockView.tick() = recorded T during R3/R4; first RUNNING tick T+1) and clear half (b); R3 restore(data, stored_version, ctx) or default_state-through-restore per WORLD persisted block in DAG order; R4 post_restore(ctx) per WORLD persisted and non-persisted block in the same order; R5 uncached state_hash verdict (diagnostic only); R6 binding rebuild; R7 load_seq+1, one ALL batch per block, snap_baseline, RUNNING via load_done. New game: N3 default_state for every non-PROFILE block, N4 init_world in DAG order under one INIT scope, N5 post_restore, N6 rebind, N7 load_done. First fault in R3/R4/N3-N5/R6 stops the pass: FAULTED via load_failed with LoadFailure{kind, stage, block_id, code, detail}, no tick, no command, no snapshot, no ALL batch, load_seq unchanged, half (b) empty; exits only via request_restore / request_new_game. init_world only in N4, never in a restore. changed_region after a restore is advisory; version_epoch is authoritative. Cold-open pass kind deferred to the first PROFILE block."

    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"binding_source_payload","entry_yaml":"  - contract: binding_source_payload
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed

    signal_signature: "BlockDescriptor.binding_source(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken; pure read valid at any boundary (R6/N6 after every post_restore, and ADR-0002 STRICT_DEBUG BINDING_DRIFT during RUNNING); ctx.put(a NEW PackedInt64Array [player_id, entity_id, ...] on every call, never a member) strictly ascending by (player_id, entity_id), player_id >= 1; kernel walks sources in ascending String(block_id) fixed once at the freeze by CanonicalEncoder.sorted_string_keys (the kernel compares no StringName); conflicts: BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT (domain 0 code 3, existing) with detail reason CONFLICT_OWNER | DUPLICATE_TRIPLE | SHAPE | ORDER | PLAYER_RANGE | SOURCE_FAULT"
    referenced_by:

    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"post_restore_write_policy","entry_yaml":"  - contract: post_restore_write_policy
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: every-block-owner
    consumers:
      - command-simulation-layer
      - save-load
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    signal_signature: "restore copies by value and owns nothing in the payload (Packed*Array via duplicate(), nested containers via duplicate(true), never retain data). post_restore(ctx) rebuilds the owner's derived members only: no persisted column write (except a REBASE_BLOCKS member's documented normalisation), no write to another block (REFUSED in the RESTORE scope), no clamp, prune, repair or default, no submit (SnapshotContext has none), no re-registration with another block; a fault only for a numbered verifier check; drift (e.g. IA_RESTORE_SUBJECT_DRIFT) is detected there and repaired by the owner's ordinary hook rule, a no-op on consistent state, with no first-run-after-restore flag. Reads: Tier S (persisted-answerable, incl. kernel.clock T and world_seed from R2) of any block; Tier D (needs post_restore) only of DAG predecessors; restore reads Tier S of closure predecessors only and derives no simulation state from T (a structural stamp comparison with T is allowed)."
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"restore_verifier_contract","entry_yaml":"  - contract: restore_verifier_contract

Fault names <DOMAIN>_RESTORE_<REASON> (restore) and <DOMAIN>_VERIFY_<INV> (cross-block post_restore). First failure wins; the numbered list V1..V16 is in ADR-0016 section 5.3 (V3 = the thirteen steps of ADR-0011 section 7.2 incl. the hook-cursor check, local code 26 RESTORE_HOOK_CURSOR; V7 decodes with GraphView.step_no() derived from the clock; V12 quotes INV-4 as at most one Body pose row per body and every row's body is live)."

    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"rebase_blocks_list","entry_yaml":"  - contract: rebase_blocks_list

    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"restore_order_tiebreak","entry_yaml":"  - decision: restore_order_tiebreak
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    api: "restore, post_restore, default_state and init_world all follow one DAG order: Kahn over restore_after, ready list ordered by registration index, smallest ready index first (the rule of the hook sort, ADR-0003 section 8); unknown id UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY, cycle or self edge RESTORE_CYCLE (18), more than MAX_BLOCKS BLOCK_LIMIT (19), all boot failures; duplicate entry is a boot warning; bind_order is built once at the freeze with CanonicalEncoder.sorted_string_keys"
    reason: "One algorithm and one total order that is a pure function of registration data; the permutation test (KRN-RST-05) catches any dependency not declared in restore_after"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"default_state_through_restore","entry_yaml":"  - decision: default_state_through_restore
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    api: "A persisted block's default_state(ctx) ends with ctx.put(payload) of snapshot shape and current schema_version; the kernel moves the payload out of the put-slot, clears the slot, then applies it by calling that block's own restore (which copies by value); no put is DEFAULT_STATE_NO_PAYLOAD (21); a non-persisted block's default_state only resets derived members"
    reason: "One copy path validates every default on every new game and every absent-block restore; clearing the slot means re-arming never leaves a stale payload"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"post_restore_cross_block_write","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: post_restore_cross_block_write
    status: active           # ADR-0016 is Proposed
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    description: "A post_restore (or restore) that calls another owner's mutator or opens another block's WriteScope, including re-registering subjects with another block. The RESTORE scope opens the restoring block only; the attempt is REFUSED and counted as WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE. Cross-block repair belongs to the owner's ordinary hook. Enforced at run time by the RESTORE scope and test KRN-RST-08 (no lint pack)."
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"post_restore_clamp_or_prune","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: post_restore_clamp_or_prune

    description: "Clamping, pruning, repairing or defaulting a persisted value in restore or post_restore. A structurally bad value is a ctx.fault; a well-formed but dead reference restores as it is and is handled by the next hook run. The only writes of persisted state in post_restore are the documented normalisations of REBASE_BLOCKS members."

      - docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md

Restore checks are structural only (shape, range, id order, reference resolution, physical ceilings, persisted-stamp comparisons); an unresolved def_id is structural."

    revised: """},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"restore_retains_payload_reference","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: restore_retains_payload_reference

  api: "pending bytes on emitter and subject rows, a pending anchor pair, hdr.last_place_tick, and the closed TRANSITIONS_PENDING table: a mutator that runs after emitter.place in its tick stays out of the subject table until the next run; post_restore builds the applied view and derives at last_place_tick over end-of-tick upstream state; registrations restore verbatim and drift is repaired by the registrant's first hook run, never written from post_restore"
  not: "a restore that cold-builds the table from every row; a mutator call from post_restore"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0017-emitter-state-and-integer-light-exposure-query.md
  reason: "hooks ordered after emitter.place (Interaction, Horror) call E3/E6/E7/E8; without canonical pending state a snapshot at that tick breaks save-equivalence"
  referenced_by:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0017-emitter-state-and-integer-light-exposure-query.md
  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"emitter_work_units","entry_yaml":"- purpose: emitter_work_units
  status: active
  api: "counted work units (REJ, CONE, CON, SEG, RECTS, POSE, DER, TAB, PUB, DELTA, BROAD, FRAME, RLIT, CELL) through an injected WorkCounter (Null in shipped builds) equal to the D.14 closed form under CNT-04; an always-on integer tally feeds the release counter emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling; weights are EmitterTuning data; counts never branch the simulation"
  not: "wall-clock governors; skipping or deferring mandatory work; conditional compilation"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0017-emitter-state-and-integer-light-exposure-query.md
  reason: "a time-based governor is nondeterministic; a ceiling is a counter, not a deferral"
  referenced_by:

  added: 2026-10-29
  revised: """},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"physics_or_render_occlusion_query","entry_yaml":"- pattern: physics_or_render_occlusion_query

  referenced_by_add:
    - docs/architecture/adr-0017-emitter-state-and-integer-light-exposure-query.md   # emitter.place share of the 2.0 ms P3 target (whole-hook ledger row, CT-20)"}]},{"adr":"ADR-0018","items":[{"section":"api_decisions","name":"light_origin_lattice","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: light_origin_lattice
    status: active           # ADR-0018 is Proposed; B is the design of record pending lighting spike step 3b and SO-P10; acceptance conditional on ADR-0009 F1
    api: "Every Light2D node position is Placement.at(...) or the emitter anchor (an integer cell) plus Placement.CELL_CENTRE (0.5, 0.5), written only through Placement.put_light_origin(node: Light2D, p: Vector2i); occluder polygon vertices stay on the integer corners of the OCCLUDES_LIGHT occupied spans (x0, y0)..(x1_occ + 1, y1_occ + 1) with CULL_DISABLED, closed true and no shift; shadow origin == render(EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin) at rest; a shadow-casting light anchor's cell centre is never inside an OCCLUDES_LIGHT box (SHO-07)"
    not: "Placement.put or any other writer of a Light2D position; a polygon shifted by -1/2; CULL_CLOCKWISE or CULL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE on occluder nodes; a tolerance-only shadow agreement with no origin identity; a shadow-casting light anchored inside an occluder box"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    reason: "Sim cell n is centred on n, render pixel n spans [n, n+1): an integer node sits on the cell corner, 0.707 px off and on the polygon face when the foot touches a wall (probed 2026-10-29: 3-10x more mismatches than the half-cell lattice, whole regions flip on a face)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"beam_apex_offset_and_mode","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: beam_apex_offset_and_mode
    status: active           # ADR-0018 is Proposed; OFFSET_FRAME LOCAL probed on one machine, spike step 3b confirms
    api: "The beam PointLight2D sits at the occlusion origin (foot, lattice) and Lighting writes PointLight2D.offset every render frame, write-on-change, as BeamOffset.offset_for(theta_read_back_from_node, vx, vy, ax, ay) = Vector2(vx, vy).rotated(-theta) - Vector2(ax, ay) (v = (0,0) for non-beams); beam_offset_writer.gd parameters are typed PointLight2D; mode LightingTuning.SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE {FOOT_OFFSET 0, CHEST_NODE 1} chosen once at setup (value 2 and the Emitter OCC_ORIGIN_MODE row and combination invariant arrive together with outcome D); the shadow-reach occluder set is measured from the apex and is necessary but not sufficient; ladder B, then B-pad (texture padded so the quad contains the foot), then A (control), then D; C rejected"
    not: "offset written by the Presenter or from a cached rotation; a Light2D-typed offset writer; a Light2D parented to a rotating node; a second shadow-casting light per beam; a per-frame branch on the mode; an Emitter OCC_ORIGIN_MODE row or combination invariant before outcome D"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    reason: "Probed 2026-10-29: the shadow origin follows the node and ignores offset and rotation, offset is node-local and unscaled, the apex lands within float32 at five angles, B has zero mismatches at six AC-57 offsets on a centred 1200x1200 texture while a chest node renders black; occluder culling by the real edge-apex quad is untested (SO-P10)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"beam_light_parent_body_root","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: beam_light_parent_body_root
    status: active           # ADR-0018 is Proposed; attach path owned by ADR-0034 (CT-32)
    api: "The beam PointLight2D's parent is the translation-only BodyRoot of BodyView.body_of_actor(actor), attached through BodyScenes namespace LIGHTING keyed by the seat's beam id; stage 0 BODY_TRANSFER reparents it with reparent(p, false) before stage AVATAR (2); the owning Presenter rewrites the position from BodyView.pos_x/pos_y the same frame; dev counter shadow_origin_wrong_frame is zero (SHO-04)"
    not: "parenting the beam light to the avatar, the tool layer or a rotating node; a projector write of a foreign node's position; leaving the light in the old body root after a pod hop or weld rebase"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    reason: "A wrong parent root for one frame shifts the drawn origin by the inter-body canvas offset: the drawn-against-simulated lie SO-1 exists to prevent"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"interfaces","name":"shadow_origin_pure_functions","entry_yaml":"  - contract: shadow_origin_pure_functions
    status: active
    producer: lighting (src/presentation/lighting/)
    consumers:
      - avatar-presenter
      - lighting
      - shadow-origin-probe-pack
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    signal_signature: "BeamOffset.offset_for(theta: float, vx: int, vy: int, ax: float, ay: float) -> Vector2 (pure, no Node, allocation-free); ShadowOrigin.render_origin(p: Vector2i) -> Vector2 = Vector2(p) + Placement.CELL_CENTRE; ShadowOrigin.Mode {FOOT_OFFSET, CHEST_NODE} (OCC_PUBLISHED added by the outcome-D amendment)"
    pattern: direct_call
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"light2d_position_outside_put_light_origin","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: light2d_position_outside_put_light_origin
    status: active
    description: "A Light2D position is written only by Placement.put_light_origin (integer cell plus CELL_CENTRE); Placement.put, position =, global_position = and relative-move calls on a Light2D are banned (lint SHO-01); PointLight2D.offset only in beam_offset_writer.gd (SHO-02). The Node2D write allow-list gains both entries."
    why: "An integer node sits on the cell corner and, next to a wall, on the polygon face; probed 2026-10-29 the shadow classification then differs from the simulation's segment test by 3-10x more cells."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"occluder_cull_mode_not_disabled","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: occluder_cull_mode_not_disabled
    status: active
    description: "Builder-owned OccluderPolygon2D nodes use CULL_DISABLED with integer vertices, closed true; pooled LightOccluder2D set sdf_collision false and explicit masks; CULL_CLOCKWISE and CULL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE are banned (asserted in ADR-0028's occluder-builder tests, formerly SHO-05/SHO-06)."
    why: "Probed 2026-10-29: CULL_CLOCKWISE leaks light through walls for lights outside them (35.94 % of cells wrong with the chest outside the wall); it is not a repair for a light inside a footprint."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"chest_node_for_beam_shadow_without_ac57","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: chest_node_for_beam_shadow_without_ac57
    status: active
    description: "The beam Light2D is not positioned at the chest point (outcome A) unless lighting spike step 3b records every AC-57 row passing; the default is the foot-lattice node with an offset-carried apex (outcome B), with B-pad tried before A."
    why: "A chest node inside or beyond a wall footprint renders black or leaks (probed 2026-10-29: 27 % to 66 % of cells wrong for s <= 20, a black beam at s = 20)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"shadow_light_anchored_inside_occluder","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: shadow_light_anchored_inside_occluder
    status: active
    description: "A shadow-casting light anchor whose cell centre (p + CELL_CENTRE) lies inside any OCCLUDES_LIGHT box is demoted to non-shadow or fails content validation (SHO-07)."
    why: "With CULL_DISABLED a shadow-casting light inside a closed occluder polygon renders the whole view dark (probed 2026-10-29, luminance 0.00)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"sim_motion_interpolation","entry_yaml":"  # api_decisions purpose: sim_motion_interpolation -> append to referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md   # adds Placement.CELL_CENTRE and put_light_origin (registry row ~971 to be amended via ADR-0009 F1)"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"presentation_stage_order","entry_yaml":"  # interfaces contract: presentation_stage_order -> append to referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md   # depends on AVATAR (2) before LIGHTING (6) for the offset ordering, and stage 0 before AVATAR for the beam light reparent"}]},{"adr":"ADR-0034","items":[{"section":"state_ownership","name":"projector_scene_tree","entry_yaml":"  - state: projector_scene_tree
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed
    owner_system: layout projector and body.projector (src/presentation/projector/)

    referenced_by:

    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: """},{"section":"interfaces","name":"projector_attach_api","entry_yaml":"  - contract: projector_attach_api
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: body.projector

Foreign bands: Marks, Mounted, PropsActors, Dust; Floor, Faces and Caps are projector-only; the projector sets z, owners never write z_index. Foreign attachments are parked in Staging before any root is freed and on_orphaned is called when their body or section is gone. Mutation facade only, an ADR-0009 section 1 exception requested"
    referenced_by:

    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: """},{"section":"interfaces","name":"camera_limits_sink","entry_yaml":"  - contract: camera_limits_sink
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed; ADR-0008 is asked to consume it and to own rect_eff and the clamp rules
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: body.projector (stage PROJECT)

    referenced_by:

    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: """},{"section":"interfaces","name":"entity_id_namespaces","entry_yaml":"  - contract: entity_id_namespaces
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: src/shared/entity_id.gd and entity_ns.gd (L0)
    consumers:

    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    signal_signature: "EntityId.pack(ns: int, local: int) -> int = (ns << 56) | local, ns 1..127; EntityNs LAYOUT 1, BODY 2, INTERACTION 3, HORROR 4, SUIT 5, WEB 6, TRAIL 7, LIGHTING 8 (a BodyScenes registration key, never a sort key), 9..127 reserved; the table is append-only with a golden test, never renumbered, and is not an acceptance condition; layout_local(section_id, kind_ordinal, idx) = (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | idx with kind_ordinal DOOR_LEAF 1, PROP 2, MACHINE 3, BEAD 4, PLATE 5, SCAR 6, JAMB 7 (numbers assigned here, vocabulary owned by ADR-0013). A presentation sort-key composite, never a block id, never persisted"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"y_sort_scope_merged","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: y_sort_scope_merged
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed; probed 2026-10-29 on the 4.7.2 editor binary, release export UNVERIFIED (SP-YSORT-1)
    api: "World and every BodyRoot are y_sort_enabled; nested y_sort_enabled nodes form one merged sort scope keyed by accumulated transform; equal keys tie by tree order; a TileMapLayer cell key = cell_top + tile_size.y/2 + TileData.y_sort_origin + TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin + layer.position.y (texture size irrelevant); same-row cells of one layer tie by x, independent of set_cell order; wall-face and wall-mounted layers use cell height WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH and a layer y_sort_origin of WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH/2; class rank is the order of the sorted groups Faces < Mounted < PropsActors; in every group the TileMapLayers are a prefix of the child list in ascending section_id (LayerOrder), followed by sprites in (class_rank, entity_id) order via SortedLayer with index base layers.count()"
    not: "a non-sorting BodyRoot (sorts its subtree as one unit); tie-break by creation order or mount order; copying y_sort_origin 24 without the cell height; two atlas sources in one TileMapLayer; tile layers ordered by weld history"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    reason: "Probed: nested sorting nodes merge by global key, ties follow tree order, tile key is measured from the cell centre; reparent appends the node as last child so layer order must be restored by section_id; two atlas sources alternating by row read 440 draw calls in an unsorted layer and 23 when sorted"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"z_band_names","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: z_band_names
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed
    api: "ZBand FLOOR 0, MARKS 1, YSORT 10, CAPS 20, DUST 30 in src/presentation/projector/z_band.gd; z_index is written only by the group builder; dependents use names; every light's range_z_min <= FLOOR and range_z_max >= DUST (default -1024..1024 probed inclusive); fallback table 0, 1, window 10..899, 900, 910 is specified, not built"
    not: "a z number outside z_band.gd; a presenter writing z_index; a trail on z 0 or +20; a Y-sorted floor, cap or dust node"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    reason: "The order of the bands is the contract (PR-5); Light2D range_z excludes items outside it (probed)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"scene_move_primitive","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: scene_move_primitive
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed; ADR-0009 is asked to reword its reparent sanction
    api: "SceneMove.to(node, new_parent) = node.reparent(new_parent, false) is the only way presentation changes a node's parent; the local position is kept (probed), the node becomes the last child, LayerOrder and SortedLayer restore order; positions are recomputed through Placement.put; on 4.7.2 reparenting or showing a TileMapLayer makes the engine rebuild every cell once, deferred (about 0.9 us per cell on the dev machine), and that rebuild is the weld budget term R_weld"
    not: "Node.reparent(parent) with the default keep_global_transform = true (rewrites the local position); freeing a node another presenter attached; treating the reparent call time as the weld cost; position + delta arithmetic for sprites"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    reason: "TR-shipbody-032 forbids global-transform-preserving reparent; Placement.put is the one integer assignment point; probe V10 shows the rebuild lands in the deferred update"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"merged_per_body_tilemaplayer","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: merged_per_body_tilemaplayer
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed
    description: "One TileMapLayer per body holding the cells of several sections, or two TileSetAtlasSource in one layer."
    why: "Welded sections sit on a 24 px grid offset (the MVP pair is 14.5 tiles) so cells cannot share a 48 px grid, which alone settles it; a salvage would also rebuild the whole body, and a second atlas source is a draw-call risk (440 calls in an unsorted probe, 23 when sorted)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    added: 2026-10-29"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"one_arg_node_reparent","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: one_arg_node_reparent
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed
    description: "Calling Node.reparent with one argument (global-transform-preserving) anywhere in presentation; every parent change goes through SceneMove."

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

# Architecture Decision Registry
#
# PURPOSE: Single source of truth for key architectural stances that all ADRs
# must agree on. Skills check this before writing new ADRs to detect conflicts
# at authoring time — before stories are created against contradictory decisions.
#
# RULES:
#   - Register a stance when it constrains how OTHER systems must be built.
#     An internal implementation detail that affects only one ADR does not need
#     to be registered.
#   - Never delete entries — set status: "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN" instead,
#     quoted: unquoted, the second colon makes the file invalid YAML.
#   - When a stance changes: update the entry, set revised: to today's date,
#     add a comment with the old value, and run /architecture-review to check
#     what ADRs are now invalidated.
#   - adr: is the authoritative source. All other ADRs that depend on this
#     stance list themselves in referenced_by.
#
# WRITTEN BY: /architecture-decision (Phase 5 — after ADR is approved)
# READ BY:    /architecture-decision (Step 2 — before authoring begins)
#             /architecture-review (Phase 4 — cross-ADR conflict baseline)
#             /create-stories (to embed architectural constraints in stories)
#             /dev-story (to check implementation against accepted stances)
#
# SEARCH PATTERNS (for skills using Grep):
#   All state owners:       Grep pattern="^  - state:" path="docs/registry/architecture.yaml"
#   Who owns player_health: Grep pattern="state: player_health"
#   All signal contracts:   Grep pattern="pattern: signal"
#   Budget for combat:      Grep pattern="system: combat"
#   All forbidden patterns: Grep pattern="^  - pattern:" (forbidden_patterns section)
#   Superseded entries:     Grep pattern="superseded_by: ADR-"
#
# LAYOUT: the one shape .claude/scripts/registry.sh reads. Each section is a
#   key at column 0 holding a block list, or [] while it is empty. Each entry
#   starts with its section's name key ("- state:", "- contract:", "- system:"
#   or "- target_fps:" for the frame budget, "- purpose:", "- pattern:"), the
#   dash at column 2 (or 0, the same for every entry of a section); its fields
#   sit two columns past the dash. Quote a value that holds ": ", such as
#   "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN". A line in any other shape is reported as
#   unsupported layout, with its number.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.
